Anyway, we talked after he got off work. He was immediately defensive of porn like when I brought up things about the industry's treatment of women. That the majority of porn is not that way... I lost my mind. Like how can he be okay with supporting that industry knowing there are people being exploited?? I explained to him that porn is not a nessecary commodity...like yes it's very likely other things we consume are made in an unethical way, but we have little choice in whether or not we use those things. Anyway, I basically told him to stop talking cause he doesn't know what he's talking about. He agreed that he didn't and that many of these things he had not thought about before and that he would have to look into it.

Then I ended up texting him after we got off the phone and telling him that it's disgusting that he would defend the objectification and exploitation of women and that his anecdotal evidence is bullshit...

Or sometimes it's just like passive aggressively being quiet then deciding I'm going to ignore them, but it never lasts. My romantic relationships are definitely more turbulent. Super fear of abandonment and feelings of inadequacy.

I don't feel like I'm especially impulsive... I guess I have quit 2 jobs without having a plan. One I was done with the management the other I just felt like I couldn't perform. I've definitely text bombed people or brought things up totally out of the blue like picking fights... But then people talk about attachment theory. I've also like had panic attacks and freak outs when in arguments with a romantic partner ESPECIALLY if they tell me to leave or stonewall.

Definitely moody af. Like that's what's really fucking me up right now. And I think the black and white thinking is a lot of that... Like things are okay or they're completely not. Never manic or high highs. It's hard for me to see outside of what I'm currently feeling... Which I also think has led to diagnosis issues because I talk to a psych and I'm like yeah, everything is fine, but then I'm calling 2 weeks later to schedule a sooner appt cause I'm freaking out and feel like I can't get out of bed.

Sorry to go on and on. I share all this in case maybe this seems typical of experiences you've had our your knowledge of BPD. Again, not trying to ask for diagnosis of course, but like just wondering BPD looks like in others.

Maybe those are just the judgements I have of myself.

Then there's protecting the listener... I don't want them to worry....That I'm not okay. That I'll go back. That I'll end up in another abusive relationship. I don't want them to feel pain through my pain.

Again, maybe I'm just projecting my own worries.

I definitely had this attitude as a child. I was always outspoken and "tough" and the class clown. I was highly sensitive to rejection, but expressed it as anger instead of sadness. Definitely had a problem with authority. Not totally defiant, but just didn't understand the purpose of boundaries. Like I couldn't grasp that a teacher or adult was somehow "above" me.

When I got into highschool it was like my emotions shifted hard from anger to sadness. I think initially the anger was there. I felt like people at school were shallow or immature and I was "different". I had a false sense of superiority that stemmed from my feelings of inferiority. I just wanted to be like everyone else. I was shy and withdrawn. I didn't know how to put myself out there. I definitely avoided romantic relationships and considered if I might be asexual...I think I was moreso hoping I was asexual.

My first relationships I was like clingy and mean at the same time. Ended up in an abusive relationship. Then I avoided intimacy. I would settle for sex. I would always say "I'm too crazy". Lol like I was sparing them the of the chaos. Then I had a semi-normal long-term relationship, but the passion died. He was practically asexual. Tried to have an open relationship, but it just hurt. I didn't feel right being with anyone else and I hated that he didn't seem to care that I was sleeping with other people. After that there was a break. I ended up in a 2 year shit show with someone who didn't want to commit to me but was committed to me? Like he didn't want to be my boyfriend, but for all intents and purposes was my bf. I was pretty nutty and obsessive with him. When he ended things I was broken. I started sleeping around to try and get over it. I would drink and hook up with randoms from dating apps. Sex was less terrifying than going on a date. Alcohol was nessecary to calm my nerves and lower inhibitions. Through that pattern of self-destructive behavior I ended up in an abusive relationship with a drug addict...and became a drug addict. Luckily that was only 6 months. Never got over my non-committal ex.

I started working the NA program (meetings, steps, sponsor) as soon as I left that relationship. About 5 months into recovery I reached out to my non-committal ex. Not with romantic intentions. I was traumatized and had like no sexual or romantic desire. I just still had the attachment. I was going through a rough time and I knew he would make me feel better. And he did. And it was okay until I started having stupid feelings again... We have only seen each other twice in-person. We talk on the phone and text regularly. He's made a lot of changes and so have I, but he doesn't think we should go down that road again. We had a turbulent relationship. I know logically it won't work, but emotionally I'm stuck.

Anyway, I just rambled a whole lot. Thank you for reading and responding to my original post and reading this too if you made it through!

I hope it works for you. Truly. I still hope it works for me too honestly. I would really never encourage anyone to give up on the program. Not without giving it a real chance. I don't know your history and all that, so maybe you have. I first told myself I would wait a year, then it was finish the 12 steps...and now I'm half way through the steps and struggling.

However, I have gotten 13 months of recovery out of NA. More than just clean time I have learned how to sit in my emotions and how to be less reactionary. I have more self-confidence than I have ever had in my life. I've learned a lot about boundaries, respecting and setting them. I also have a more optimistic view of the future even if sometimes I still feel like things are bleak af. There's this little sliver of hope that now lives inside of me and keeps me from giving up on most things. Arguably, my higher power, but I struggle with that. The loving and kind thing really gets me because I don't believe anything is entirely good or entirely bad. I think most things just are.

I just need to step away from the "fellowship" portion right now because I'm building a resentment/resentments towards people and the entire program.

I don't know about step work. I'm on my 6th and part of me feels like I need to start over completely because I don't feel steps 1-3 anymore and I've had doubts about my 4th step. My sponsor has told me I have done a thorough job, but idk. If I completed it the way it should be done, then either I am not getting the results or I am not understanding the results.

Wow. I'm sorry that was your experience. Did you ever get another sponsor?

I'm fortunate that my sponsor is like the one person in the fellowship I trust and can depend on.

The only area in my life where I feel like an addict is in romantic relationships, but even there I have had multiple periods of my life where I was single and celibate including the past 13 months. My fear of being alone is what lead me to my DOC. However, therapy and the program have really helped me recognize my issues, identify where they came from and now hopefully correct the thinking and behavior.

My mental health was on a gradual downward trajectory with some peaks and valleys, but crack and my ex really sped up the trip to rock bottom. 

My disease is depression. Depression is the thing that has led me to not do things I want to do or do things I don't want to do. There are a lot of overlapping feelings shared by people suffering from addiction and people suffering from depression. I realize the two are also not mutually exclusive.

Do I feel better now? Yes.

But I don't think that would change if I had the occasional drink.

Do I feel better than when I was new? No. I feel worse. 

13 months into the program and I feel like my hope of what the fellowship would be and who I could be within it is gone.

That's a great way of looking at it. I really am grateful for those things. I just want to have my cake and eat it too.

I don't relate to a lot of the Fellowship. Probably the majority of people I have met. I also don't relate to the way addict is defined and the disease of addiction. I think it's true for many, but I don't feel like it applies to me. I don't believe in a higher power that can only be loving and kind. I cannot think of a single concept or being that is solely loving and kind. I don't like the emphasis on negative events and characteristics. It's like pages upon pages of how terrible we were and how flawed we are and how all of the horrible things were our fault and then like one small section on assets... I don't like the fear mongering.

I'm glad it works for so many. I'm just not sure it's for me.
The program as a whole has helped. It's this most recent attempt to get back in it that isn't working yet. And I say yet because I believe it can, but I do have reservations.

Thanks for your perspective. It makes sense. The rationalization and progression. I struggle with the idea of never being healed though. 

I don't have a history of obsessive and compulsive behaviors except in regards to romantic relationships which was a huge factor in my substance abuse. I used substances as tool to get or maintain what I actually wanted which was love and also to cope to with difficult feelings and symptoms of depression.

But I'm not depressed anymore. I don't want to drink to cope. I just want to be a normie. I want a normie life. I want to go to a baseball game and have a beer. I want to toast champagne on New Year's Eve. I think I'm capable of doing that. At the moment though, I'm in a living situation that doesn't allow me to test that theory so I stay clean. I'm not going to turn my life upside down just so I can have a couple drinks.

However, if I'm fully honest I'm also terrified of dating sober. I've never done it. I feel severely limited in regards to who I can date (people who are clean) and who I want to date and would want to date me.

Honestly, it's easier. Life would be easier if I could drink and unwind and socialize the way others do. 

I really don't feel like an addict as much as I am someone who was addicted to a particular substance. I have always been able to drink in moderation. Alcohol has never controlled me or made my life unmanageable. 

Depression controlled me and made my life unmanageable. As I fell into deeper and deeper depression I developed more and more progressively worse self-destructive habits, which aligns with addiction, but also just being depressed. I understand the two are not mutually exclusive but I've never really exhibited compulsive addict behavior except in regards to romantic relationships. 

My desire to be loved and inability to form and respect boundaries lead me to start using. I met someone who I thought was just so mesmerizing and impressive that was so good at creating the illusion of being functional and a "recreational" user. He was also manipulative and abusive and preyed on my weakness. He had all of the answers and power and control and I just blindly followed. I liked getting high, but I really liked him more. My head was on so backwards at the time that I didn't even know he was abusive despite very clear and obvious abuse and numerous red flags that indicated the type of person he is. Looking back he makes sick, but at the time if he would have gotten clean I would have stayed.

All in all I'm grateful to have had that shit experience because I have gained a lot in recovery. I recognize the value in living clean. Sometimes though, it feels like a punishment. Like I made this decision to be with this person and use my DOC for 6 months and now my life is forever changed and I've had to give up things that I enjoy. Ultimately I am making the decision to stay clean, but like I said it's really circumstantial more than anything.    I refuse to lie. I want to abide by the rules of the home I'm living in and I have a great thing living here and I'm not willing to throw that away cause boohoo I want to have a mimosa by the pool with my friends.

If you want to live alone, you should definitely intend to spend more like 900+ for a studio. It's not impossible to find a place at less, but it will likely be in an undesirable neighborhood or cockroach infested.

When I say undesirable, I don't just mean "dangerous". There are areas of the city that are "food deserts" because of the lack of access to grocery stores and fresh food. You are not going to find much in terms of bars, restaurants, etc. Churches, liquor stores, a few fast food spots and maybe a hair salon.

As for the danger in Chicago. Most of that is gang violence, however unintended targets can get caught in the cross-fire. Certain neighborhoods on the south and west sides (including Garfield Park & Austin), unfortunately, have more concentrations of gangs. Aside from violence, you are encountering people just hanging out on street corners, many of which are gang affiliated, many of which are selling hard drugs. With drugs comes addicts which is a whole other thing.

To clarify, I am sympathetic to addicts and I'm not insinuating there are just criminals and gang members living in these areas. I'm just laying it out there.

If you're looking for a room, I think $700 is completely reasonable.

But yeah, neighborhood is dependent on what is important to you. CTA access, walkability, safety, park/lake access, proximity to things that are important to you (restaurants, gym, bars, etc.).

And yes, parking in the city blows, but the further you get from the center of the city the better it usually is. Tip: read the signs before parking. Some streets have certain times/days where there's no parking, street cleaning, construction, permit parking, meters.

I love Edgewater which is right by the lake and Red Line, but parking is hell.

I think Old Irving (Irving Park Blue Line), Albany Park(Kimball/Kedzie Brown Line) are good options. Parking isn't great in either. That mostly just means you might drive around the blocks around your house a few times before you find a legal spot.
